Predicates:
GoodGuys(x) ::: x are good guys.
Win(x, y) ::: x wins y.
Fight(x, y) ::: x fights y.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
Character(x) ::: x is a character.
InMovie(x, y) ::: x is in the movie y.
Nemesis(x, y) ::: x is the nemesis of y.
Fights(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Movie(y) ::: y is a movie.
Title(y, z) ::: y is the title of z.
Year(y, z) ::: y was published in year z.
Specialize(x, y) ::: x specializes in y.
Author(x, y) ::: x is the author of y.
Book(y) ::: y is a book.
Publish(y, z) ::: y is published in year z.
Miro(x) ::: x is Miroslav Venhoda.
Music(y) ::: y is music.
Love(x, y) ::: x loves y.

Premises:
∀x (SuperheroMovie(x) → ∃y (Character(y) ∧ NamedAfter(x, y))) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a character.
SuperheroMovie(theSurprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
NamedAfter(theSurprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar, SirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
Character(SirDigby) ::: Sir Digby is a character.
Title(theSurprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar, "The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar") ::: The movie is titled as such.
Fights(SirDigby, nemesis) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
∃x (Fights(x, y) → ¬Win(x, y)) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they fight does not win.
InMovie(SirDigby, theSurprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar) ::: Sir Digby is in the movie.
InMovie(nemesis, theSurprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar) ::: The nemesis is in the movie.
∃x (Win(x, y) ∧ Fight(x, y)) ::: Somebody wins a fight.
∀x, y (Fight(x, y) → Fight(y, x)) ::: Good guys fight bad guys and vice versa.
GoodGuys(x) ::: x are good guys.
∀x (InMovie(x, theSurprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar) → Character(x)) ::: If someone is in the movie, they are a character.

Conclusion:
¬Win(nemesis, SirDigby) ::: The nemesis of Sir Digby does not win.
